title: British support for jazz
summary: Freeman says Britons have backed American dance music and jazz for seventy years and turn out seriously for American soloists.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, that's right. Well, of course, in your case it's very much better because you're at home. You know, when you're off, you're at home.

Yes, I have a lot of -- well, I know everybody in London, and I know so many people throughout the U.K. and I played -- I must have played in the 16 years I have been coming here on and off, I must have played 100 cities, you know, and they are all jazz -- you know, you must
realize the British have been supporting American music, that would be dance music and jazz for some 70 years, and the Prince of Wales, Edward the VIII was an amateur drummer.
Yes, I remember, Prince George too.

Yes, and the British really love jazz. I mean, they are quite serious about it. They do turn out for a wellknown American soloist, and the British have some damned good players now themselves. They have been dedicated to music.
